transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-30 09:00 PDT
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Participants: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Das (Redwood CSM), Maya Singh (Aurelia Head of Cloud), Tom Reynolds (Aurelia Platform Eng), Aditi Rao (Aurelia CISO), Eric Long (Aurelia VP Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood + Aurelia alignment on priority account play. Primary asks: predictable throughput for inference, on-prem/VPC constraints, compliance and SSO, and clear co-sell responsibilities. Agreement to run short benchmark on Aurelia infra and exchange SOW + pricing. Next: joint exec intro and bench results.

Topics: joint account plan, Dedicated vs Hosted routing, private deployment (VPC/on-prem), security (audit logs/KMS), pricing for reserved capacity, co-sell motion and stakeholder list, pilot scope.

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript body:
00:00 - Lena Park: okay everyone thanks for carving out time this morning um this is our partner handoff for the Aurelia priority account, quick intros from our side — I'm Lena, AE, Omar is our solutions engineer and Priya will be CS.
00:15 - Maya Singh: Hi, Maya here, thanks. We've got Tom, Aditi and Eric on from Aurelia. Appreciate the handoff.
00:28 - Omar Ruiz: Great, quick agenda; we wanna confirm success criteria for the deal, technical gating items, and a short plan for a 48 hour perf run on your infra, Maya. Does that sound right?
00:42 - Tom Reynolds: Yep that sounds good. FYI our current infra is hybrid — main inference traffic in GCP but sensitive workloads live in a vpc-connected colo for latency reasons.
00:58 - Aditi Rao: And from security, we'll need SOC2 evidence, KMS key handling, and admin-level audit logs. Also SSO SAML setup must be compatible with our IdP.
01:15 - Lena Park: Totally agree — Redwood Private supports KMS and audit logs; we'll send our security pack. Quick question on scale: what are the 95th percentile latency targets and QPS expectations?
01:32 - Maya Singh: We're looking at 95th < 120ms for standard prompt paths and about 2k qps at peak for batched inference. We're also considering a lower-latency path for interactive agents.
01:46 - Omar Ruiz: 2k qps is reasonable — we'll propose a Dedicated pool sizing and also show a hosted fall back to keep continuity if capacity spikes. For latency the trick will be prefix caching and smaller batch windows for the interactive route.
02:05 - Eric Long: On the commercial side, we're evaluating reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go. What's typically the tipping point?
02:20 - Lena Park: Usually teams move to Dedicated at predictable steady-state usage; reserved gives better unit economics. We'll share a model comparing hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved cost at your expected utilization.
02:33 - Tom Reynolds: We also have an internal rule about data residency — anything with PII must stay in the colo zone. Can Redwood route by policy?
02:48 - Omar Ruiz: Yes, smart routing can pin requests by policy to your private deployment; we can run a per-tenant route so PII traffic never leaves the VPC. Quick caveat: some model variants with quantization may perform differently on on-prem hardware.
03:10 - Maya Singh: That's fine, but we'd need a performance baseline before committing.
03:18 - Lena Park: Agreed — propose 48-hour benchmark: we'll run a set of workloads with your sample prompts, measure latency, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens. Omar will prepare the runbook.
03:32 - Aditi Rao: Also need to validate our HSM/KMS flow — we don't want any key material in vendor-managed key stores.
03:44 - Omar Ruiz: Understood — Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys and HSM integrations. We'll include an architecture doc and steps for key rotation.
03:57 - Tom Reynolds: What's the troubleshooting path if we hit a tail-latency regression during the pilot?
04:05 - Priya Das: Priya here — our ops will set up tracing hooks and token-level breakdowns in the console. For incidents, we'll have a 24/7 war-room cadence during the bench and a runbook for rollbacks to fallback model variants.
04:24 - Eric Long: On the co-sell mechanics — how do we align compensation and reps? Aurelia's sales lead wants an intro to Redwood's field motion.
04:36 - Lena Park: We'll do a joint exec intro; Redwood's partner ops will propose a referral/credit structure or co-sell discount depending on contract. We'll share a draft joint account plan.
04:50 - Maya Singh: Sounds good. One thing — we've been pitched by CloudBound and Inferra; Inferra claims low-latency on CPU quantized models. How's Redwood different?
05:04 - Omar Ruiz: Short answer: runtime optimizations + smart caching + model routing. We also provide a unified API across hosted/dedicated/private so your app needs minimal changes during rollout. Also our kernel selection and KV cache behavior is tuned for those interactive tails.
05:26 - Tom Reynolds: Will we need code changes for the routing policies?
05:31 - Omar Ruiz: Minimal — it's config-first. You can pin model version or tag routes by tenant. We'll share a sample routing policy.
05:42 - Lena Park: Let's talk timeline — Maya, do you have a target procurement window?
05:48 - Maya Singh: We're aiming to finalize procurement in Q3, ideally contract signed by mid-July. The pilot needs to complete before legal finalizes terms.
06:01 - Lena Park: Okay that aligns — we'll aim to deliver benchmark results by 2026-07-06 and SOW draft by 2026-07-09.
06:10 - Aditi Rao: On compliance evidence — can you share SOC2 Type II report and ISO attestation?
06:16 - Priya Das: Yes, we'll share redacted reports and a security playbook. Also if you need additional penetration test artifacts we can coordinate.
06:28 - Tom Reynolds: For the bench, can we run it in our dev colo first? We want to ensure infra is accessible and that we don't risk prod.
06:36 - Omar Ruiz: Absolutely — dev colo sounds perfect. We'll need a small VM with GPU access or an IPA to connect to your staging inference fabric, plus sample prompts and tokenization details.
06:52 - Lena Park: Quick note on billing: for the bench we'll provide a provisional cost estimate and credits for the evaluation if the pilot turns into a contract within 30 days.
07:05 - Eric Long: The credit is helpful. Also, what about uptime SLAs for Dedicated?
07:12 - Lena Park: Our Dedicated offering includes SLA-backed uptime for reserved pools — we'll include the SLA terms in the proposal.
07:20 - Maya Singh: A couple of items from Aurelia leadership: 1) Exec intro, 2) pilot scope defined, 3) security docs delivered, 4) preliminary pricing.
07:33 - Lena Park: We'll own 1 and 3, Omar will own 2 technical bench, Priya will handle 4/proposal.
07:41 - Tom Reynolds: Anything else on data handling? We encrypt at rest and in transit; need to ensure no cached PII persists beyond TTL.
07:51 - Omar Ruiz: We can set cache TTLs and have a purge policy; we'll document KV cache retention settings. Also can offer prefix-avoidance for PII routes.
08:08 - Maya Singh: Good. Also, small ask: can Redwood support an A/B routing during pilot to compare hosted vs private?
08:20 - Omar Ruiz: Yes, can be done — weight-based routing for the window. We'll include traffic splits in the runbook.
08:30 - Eric Long: From product POV, we'll want to see structured logging and a few sample traces for debugging.
08:38 - Priya Das: We'll enable token-level logging and give access to the per-route dashboards for the pilot.
08:46 - Lena Park: OK let's move to ownership and timeline recap before closing.
09:02 - Lena Park: Recap: action items — Lena send pricing and joint account plan; Omar sends bench runbook and routing samples; Priya sends security pack and proposal template; Maya share traffic profile. Deliverables targeted first week of July.
09:20 - Maya Singh: Confirmed. One more question — do you have references for a similar regulated customer?
09:28 - Lena Park: Yes, we'll include two adopter references; one in fintech and one in healthcare. We'll anonymize specifics.
09:36 - Aditi Rao: That helps. Also, legal will want a data processing addendum.
09:42 - Lena Park: We'll include a standard DPA and can iterate.
09:47 - Eric Long: Great — thanks everyone. Any final comments?
09:52 - Tom Reynolds: No, looking forward.
09:55 - Omar Ruiz: We'll get the runbook out by Monday.
09:58 - Priya Das: I'll add the calendar invite for the bench kickoff.
10:05 - Lena Park: Thanks all, talk soon.

Meeting end.
